rulings.topic: 5 tests that mutate execution/test CSI via raw SQL, now refused by the DB for observed runs
rulings.verdict: REBUILD all 5 (no deletion). Re-seat each mutation on an execution row the final schema legitimately allows to carry that state, and keep a precondition that proves the DB refuses the same mutation on an observed row.

verified: Re-baselined V13 draft keeps ui_test_executions.csi_id nullable and states 'the application excludes every NULL-CSI row from user-facing queries' (data-draft/V13__executions_ledger.sql:126,214-216).

The V15 draft studio_observed_execution_guard returns NEW without checks when observed_revision_binding IS NULL, unless revision_id points to a GUIDED_RUN revision (data-draft/V15__publication.sql:350-354). So an unbound row's csi_id can still be NULL or changed under the final schema.

ui_tests.csi_id is FK-pinned by studio_guided_publication_bases and studio_secret_use_audit on (id, csi_id) only once those rows exist. An unpublished test with no secret audit can still have its CSI changed at the DB level.
facts.inference: The route-level CSI authorization (execution's own CSI, NULL-CSI fail-closed, SSE refresh) is path-independent code that guards states the final schema still allows. For observed rows, execution CSI always equals test CSI and neither can change, so without these discriminating tests a regression that switched the route to a parent-test CSI lookup would never be detected.

rulings.rationale: ADR-SC-005 'Preserves CSI authorization ... video/evidence/SSE'. The tests are the falsification pair and the fail-closed proof for a security control, so deleting them loses security coverage. Re-seating is not a legacy path: no production code changes, no fallback is added, and the route answers from row state that the schema allows.

rebuildSpec.seat: One named support helper (e.g. StudioExecutionFixtures.unboundExecution(testId, csi, principal, environment, status)). It inserts a ui_test_executions row (plus the ledger/evidence rows each class's control half needs) with observed_revision_binding NULL, observed_admission_receipt NULL, and revision_id NULL or an ordinaryRevision (never a GUIDED_RUN revision; the guard refuses that). For movingTheParentTestsCsiDoesNotChangeTheAnswer, the parent test must be unpublished and have no secret-use audit rows.
rebuildSpec.keepControlHalf: Each rebuilt test keeps its pre-mutation control: the same identity is served (200 or an open stream) on the unbound row before the mutation, so the after-state refusal is non-vacuous.
rebuildSpec.precondition: Each rebuilt test first asserts that the original mutation on the class's observed (bound) execution is refused by the DB (DataAccessException with 'observed execution binding invalid' for execution CSI, and an FK violation for a published test's CSI). This pins the invariant behind the re-seat. Keep it inside the existing method; do not add a new method.
rebuildSpec.stopCondition: If a route refuses or 404s an unbound row before mutation (so the control half cannot pass), STOP and return to @architect. Do not delete unilaterally and do not weaken the control.

rulings.reconciliation: Count-neutral: 5 in-place arrangement re-seats under the same names, 0 deletions, 0 ports. List them in the ledger under 'arrangementReseats' with from/to. Had deletion been chosen, the rule would have been after = baseline - 0 - 5 + 0 for those classes, and that option is rejected.
rejectedAlternatives: Delete as unreachable: wrong, because the state is still reachable for unbound rows and the code branch is live; it would also lose the route-uses-own-CSI discrimination.

Tighten V13 (csi_id NOT NULL, every execution bound) so the state becomes unreachable: a behavioural schema redesign outside the re-baseline's mandate, which would also leave the route's quarantine branch as dead code. Candidate for STUDIO-OBS-011 class-C ruling, not 012A.

rulings.topic: DispatcherIT.aRevokedAuthorizationAtDispatchIsTerminalWithAnExplicitCodeAndNoSend: no dispatch-time authorization recheck for observed runs
rulings.verdict: CONFIRMED real 012A-scope gap. Security severity HIGH. Owner: Lane K backend in 012A, not OBS-014.

verified: At HEAD StudioDispatcher.dispatchClaimed returned into dispatchObserved BEFORE calling authorization.recheck (HEAD lines 276-291). Only the artifact-1 branch was rechecked, and the baseline test passed on that branch.
The working tree removed the DispatchAuthorization field and constructor parameter from StudioDispatcher. ProvisionalDispatchAuthorization, the only implementation, now has no production consumer.

ObservedReplayAuthorization.check verifies grant expiry, scope/policy hashes, grant field equality and ledger cancel/revoke/DONE. It does NOT check that the test is deleted or quarantined, that the CSI is still registered, or that a principal is present.

ObservedReplayAuthorization.refreshRetry mints a fresh grant (TTL <= 30000 ms) after a definite refusal or zero-send outage without re-checking test lifecycle, so grant TTL does not bound exposure across retries.
observed.job(...) resolves secrets (Vault read-entry audit) before beginResolvedObservedDispatch. A check placed only in the begin transaction would still read secrets for a revoked run.

rulings.securityImpact: A soft-deleted or quarantined draft, or a de-registered CSI, still dispatches: Vault secrets are resolved and sent to the runner. That breaks AC-13a / §5.1.3 ('a permission revoked in between must stop the run ... terminal ERROR with an explicit code'). Because observed is now the only family, the control is unenforced for every run.
rulings.scopeRationale: This is a capability regression caused by 012A's deletion of the legacy branch that held the only recheck call (baseline green, now red). ADR-SC-005 keeps 'readiness/acceptance/dispatch/ledger/admission'. The fix reuses an existing interface and adds no new governance, so it does not belong to OBS-014 (new P0/P1 governance). The ADR-planned fold of GuidedPublicationAuthorization into DispatchAuthorization stays in OBS-011.

fixDesign.wiring: Re-add DispatchAuthorization as a REQUIRED constructor dependency of StudioDispatcher (both the @Autowired public constructor and the package-private test constructor), exactly as at HEAD. Do not use @Autowired(required=false): a missing authorizer must fail context start (fail closed). Spring supplies ProvisionalDispatchAuthorization. DispatcherIT's manually built dispatchers pass it explicitly, as they did at HEAD.
fixDesign.placement: In StudioDispatcher.dispatchClaimed, after the pending-deadline close and BEFORE observed.binding(...) and dispatchObserved(...), so it runs before refreshRetry, grant minting, any Vault read and any send. Every claimed attempt (first dispatch, lease-expiry re-claim, post-outage retry) passes through dispatchClaimed, so it is rechecked each time.
fixDesign.call: authorization.recheck(executionId, testId, csiId, principal). Pass csi_id as (String) row.get("csi_id") rather than String.valueOf(...), so a NULL CSI arrives as null; ProvisionalDispatchAuthorization already refuses null.
fixDesign.onRevoked: catch DispatchAuthorization.AuthorizationRevokedException -> LOGGER.warn with executionId and the fixed message only -> close(executionId, ExecutionErrorCode.AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED, now) -> return false. This is the same terminal path as HEAD and the same plain close() that dispatchObserved already uses for a refreshRetry refusal. No retry, no requeue, no secret-use no-send fact (resolution was never entered), no runner send.
fixDesign.returnValue: Discard the returned policy identity. The observed binding's currentPolicyHash is the recorded policy identity (exec-fixtures assertionRepoint for theDispatchedPolicyIdentityIsRecordedOnTheExecution). Do not write configuration_snapshot.dispatchPolicyIdentity.
fixDesign.otherExceptions: Propagate as at HEAD (the lease expires and the row is re-claimed). Do not convert them into AUTHORIZATION_REVOKED.
fixDesign.scheduledSynergy: ProvisionalDispatchAuthorization delegates to StudioScheduledDispatchAuthorization, which returns early for non-scheduled rows. That gives OBS-009 the background-grant recheck at send time with no further dispatcher change.
fixDesign.residualRisk: There is a millisecond TOCTOU window between recheck and send (a soft delete committing in between). It existed identically at HEAD and is not a regression. Do not add row locks in 012A.

rulings.tests: DispatcherIT.aRevokedAuthorizationAtDispatchIsTerminalWithAnExplicitCodeAndNoSend must pass UNCHANGED. Recommended, non-blocking: also assert zero studio_secret_use_audit rows for that execution. The full DispatcherIT, RevocationRotationIT, CancelIT and StudioDispatchMetricsIT must stay green.

rulings.topic: CONTROL_WINDOW_MARGIN_MS = 25 (runner acts earlier on a secret-bearing control window; never extends it)

verified: runCoordinator.ts:365 windowEnd = nextPoll + 1000 - CONTROL_WINDOW_MARGIN_MS, for secret-bearing runs only (non-secret runs have windowEnd null and are unaffected). requestBudget and timerBudget derive from windowEnd, so both shrink, and nothing is lengthened.
The constant is exported, documented as a latency promise and not configurable from environment or config.
Fixtures: observed-secret-control x10 consecutive went from 2/10 pass to 10/10 pass. Unit tier: 712 passed, 0 failed (control-window-margin.json). The fixtures test bound (2000 ms) is unchanged.
Root cause addressed separately: trackTree no longer blocks the event loop (runner-trackTree/ledger.json). Residual timer lateness in fixtures is 0.2-2.3 ms; probe max is 10-11 ms.

rulings.rationale: OBS-007 AC-13 requires the secret-bearing run to stop within the bound (2 s including request/queue time). Acting up to 25 ms earlier is strictly more conservative, so AC-13 semantics are preserved and tightened. The only cost is availability: an authorized control response that arrives in the last 25 ms of a 1000 ms window now stops the run (fail-closed). That is the correct direction for a secret-bearing run.
conditions: C1: Add one literal guard assertion, e.g. expect(CONTROL_WINDOW_MARGIN_MS).toBeGreaterThan(0) and toBeLessThanOrEqual(50). The current unit expectations are written in terms of the constant, so a negative value (which would extend the window) would not be caught there. This edit belongs to @dev; the architect does not make it.
C2: The constant stays a hard-coded exported constant. No env/config/Helm knob.
C3: The fixtures-tier 2000 ms bound in observed-secret-control.test.ts stays unchanged. The final-tree fixtures run is recorded with the measured cutoffs.

C4: Record the residual: the bound is met with ~25 ms headroom against observed timer lateness (max 10-11 ms in the probe). Under CPU starvation beyond that, the stop can still overrun, because Node timers are not real-time. That is a known limit and not a 012A defect. Control-endpoint latency approaching 975 ms raises spurious-stop risk; operability monitoring for that is tracked by OBS-009/GA §4.G and not here.
